## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components can approach the streaming ceiling on death-free workloads.

## Layout & approach
The AoS layout at 69 B/p offers loop 1 only 28 hot bytes (41%) — age+pos+vel — and loop 2 only 32 (47%) — color+pos+seed — leaving over half each line as dead weight. The mask intermediate adds 1 B/particle, written by loop 1 and read back by loop 2 through memory rather than kept in registers. Loop 1 is Halide-expressible; loop 2's fused scatter is not. With stride-68 access (0x44 in the disassembly), vectorization is confined to within-particle component math, not cross-particle SIMD. All measured points (N≥10000) sit past the L1d spill at N≈474 and L2 spill at N≈7598, in L3-resident or DRAM regimes.

## Cache saturation
Cost is flat across N within each death rate: q=0.01 spans 24.9–26.6 ns/p from N=10K to 10M; q=0.5 spans 30.9–33.5 ns/p. No cache-spill knee appears — neither the L2→L3 transition (N≈7598) nor L3→DRAM (N≈243K) produces a visible step. The algo is not bandwidth-limited, so cache residency does not govern cost.

## Bandwidth
Achieved 2.06–2.77 GB/s against the 12.69 GB/s ceiling — 16–22%. The memory floor is 5.437 ns/p; actual runs 4.6–6.2× above it, so irreducible memory time is a minority fraction. The algo is frontend-bound: 64–71.5% frontend stalls, 0% backend, 0% branch flush. It runs within ±3% of naive scalar (0.89–1.03× baseline) and trails the winner by 1.76–3.26×. Death rate is the primary cost axis: q=0.01 averages ~25 ns/p, q=0.5 ~33 ns/p, a ~28% rise from loop 2's branchy respawn path.

## Assembly
Loop 1 vectorizes component-wise: `vmovups` loads 16 B of position, `vshufps`/`vinsertps` rearrange components, `vmulps`/`vaddps` do 4-wide float math, `vmovlps` stores back — but one particle per iteration at stride 0x44. The mask verdict is a `setae` byte store. Loop 2 is fully scalar: `cmp BYTE PTR [r10+r15*1],0x0` checks the mask, `je` skips respawn, `call spawn` handles death, then `vcvttss2si` converts coordinates and a chain of `movzx`/`add`/`cmovae`/`mov BYTE PTR` performs byte-granular saturating adds to the framebuffer. The 411-instruction body explains the 69% frontend stall — the stream is too long and irregular for the decode pipeline.

## Verdict
Refuted — 0.89–1.03× of naive baseline (roughly par) at every N×q point, and 1.76–3.26× slower than the winner. Component-wise auto-vectorization (`vmulps`/`vaddps` within one particle) cannot overcome stride-68 AoS access: 41–47% hot bytes and one particle per iteration cap bandwidth at 16–22% of ceiling. The 69% frontend stall, driven by the 411-instruction fused step body and loop 2's byte-granular scatter, confirms the algo is frontend-bound, not memory-bound — auto-vectorization over per-particle components does not approach the streaming ceiling at any death rate.
